options.plan: Staging; upstream workforce provisioning entitlement unverified
options.region: No WorkOS or upstream region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Org-bound Okta SCIM directory; bearer auth; separate assignment/push groups; app-owned Events API bridge; no login

conditions: Select an organization-bound Okta SCIM directory in WorkOS staging and a matching bearer-token provisioning app in Okta; enable user creation, attribute updates and deactivation. OAuth client credentials are outside this selected configuration, not declared unsupported.

Okta suspension alone does not deactivate the provisioned account; deactivation/deletion has different lifecycle behavior. Verify identity mapping and application enforcement rather than equating upstream login restrictions with SaaS revocation.

WorkOS staging connections are not billed per https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments; production Directory Sync is charged per connection at https://workos.com/pricing. Upstream provisioning entitlement remains unverified; this is not free production or a zero-cost guarantee.

The application requires an Events API bridge with persisted cursor, replay handling and state reconciliation per https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/events-api. WorkOS directory data is read-only to the app, not a native SaaS SCIM endpoint or write-back path; local authorization and sessions remain application-owned.

This is a dated documentation proposal, not a tested connector or deployed bridge. Login, JIT, nested-group coverage, deprovisioning latency and complete access revocation are unverified; do not inherit another WorkOS scope's positive facts.

evidence.summary: The Okta guide documents a dedicated directory endpoint, provisioning settings and distinct suspension/deactivation behavior. This staging assertion is conditional, not a verified customer configuration.

conditions: Configure Push Groups separately from application assignment groups; assignment alone is not Group Push. Membership removal may be missing after deactivation/unassignment, so test reconciliation and explicit re-push recovery.

Okta group display names populate WorkOS idp_id; do not treat those names as immutable globally unique authorization identifiers. Bind application mapping to the intended organization, directory and WorkOS group identity.

Handle dsync.group.deleted without expecting per-member dsync.group.user_removed events per https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/understanding-events; remove that group's access without deleting unrelated memberships or user accounts.

The app-owned bridge must reconcile memberships and enforce its own permissions/sessions. This proposal covers configured group ingestion in the selected staging directory, not nested groups, login claims, production entitlement or measured revocation latency.

evidence.summary: The guide distinguishes group assignment from push configuration and records membership-removal and group-identifier limitations. Group ingestion does not prove complete application access enforcement.
